entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8385"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 4</title> <div sID="gen13426" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Isa.4.1-Isa.4.6">Is 4:1-6</reference>.<div eID="gen13426" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13427" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that day--</hi>the calamitous period described in previous chapter.<div eID="gen13427" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13428" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seven--</hi>indefinite number among the Jews. So many men would be slain, that there would be very many more women than men; for example, seven women, contrary to their natural bashfulness, would sue to (equivalent to "take hold of," <reference osisRef="Isa.3.6">Is 3:6</reference>) one man to marry them.<div eID="gen13428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13429" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eat ... own bread--</hi>foregoing the privileges, which the law (<reference osisRef="Exod.21.10">Ex 21:10</reference>) gives to wives, when a man has more than one.<div eID="gen13429" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13430" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">reproach--</hi>of being unwedded and childless; especially felt among the Jews, who were looking for "the seed of the woman," Jesus Christ, described in <reference osisRef="Isa.4.2">Is 4:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.54.1">Is 54:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.54.4">4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.1.25">Lu 1:25</reference>.<div eID="gen13430" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13431" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8385"/>2. In contrast to those on whom vengeance falls, there is a manifestation of Jesus Christ to the "escaped of Israel" in His characteristic attributes, beauty and glory, typified in Aaron's garments (<reference osisRef="Exod.28.2">Ex 28:2</reference>). Their sanctification is promised as the fruit of their being "written" in the book of life by sovereign love (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.3">Is 4:3</reference>); the means of it are the "spirit of judgment" and that of "burning" (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.4">Is 4:4</reference>). Their "defense" by the special presence of Jesus Christ is promised (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.5">Is 4:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.4.6">6</reference>).<div eID="gen13431" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13432" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">branch--</hi>the sprout of Jehovah. Messiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.5">Jr 23:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.33.15">33:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.3.8">Zec 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.6.12">6:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.1.78">Lu 1:78</reference>, Margin). The parallel clause does not, as Maurer objects, oppose this; for "fruit of the earth" answers to "branch"; He shall not be a dry, but a fruit-bearing branch (<reference osisRef="Isa.27.6">Is 27:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.23-Ezek.34.27">Eze 34:23-27</reference>). He is "of the earth" in His birth and death, while He is also "of the Lord" (Jehovah) (<reference osisRef="John.12.24">Joh 12:24</reference>). His name, "the Branch," chiefly regards His descent from David, when the family was low and reduced (<reference osisRef="Luke.2.4">Lu 2:4</reference>, 7, 24); a sprout with more than David's glory, springing as from a decayed tree (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.1">Is 11:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.53.2">53:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.16">Re 22:16</reference>).<div eID="gen13432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13433" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">excellent--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Heb.1.4">He 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.8.6">8:6</reference>).<div eID="gen13433" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13434" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">comely--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Song.5.15">So 5:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Song.5.16">16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.14">Eze 16:14</reference>).<div eID="gen13434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13435" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">escaped of Israel--</hi>the elect remnant (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.5">Ro 11:5</reference>); (<reference osisRef="1Cor.11.1">1</reference>) in the return from Babylon; (2) in the escape from Jerusalem's destruction under Titus; (3) in the still future assault on Jerusalem, and deliverance of "the third part"; events mutually analogous, like concentric circles (Zec 12:2-10; 13:8, 9, &c.; 14:2; <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.23-Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:23-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.21">Joe 3:1-21</reference>). <div eID="gen13435" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 4 Is 4:1-6 . that day-- the calamitous period described in previous chapter. seven-- indefinite number among the Jews. So many men would be slain, that there would be very many more women than men; for example, seven women, contrary to their natural bashfulness, would sue to (equivalent to "take hold of," Is 3:6 ) one man to marry them. eat ... own bread-- foregoing the privileges, which the law ( Ex 21:10 ) gives to wives, when a man has more than one. reproach-- of being unwedded and childless; especially felt among the Jews, who were looking for "the seed of the woman," Jesus Christ, described in Is 4:2 ; Is 54:1 , 4 ; Lu 1:25 . 2. In contrast to those on whom vengeance falls, there is a manifestation of Jesus Christ to the "escaped of Israel" in His characteristic attributes, beauty and glory, typified in Aaron's garments ( Ex 28:2 ). Their sanctification is promised as the fruit of their being "written" in the book of life by sovereign love ( Is 4:3 ); the means of it are the "spirit of judgment" and that of "burning" ( Is 4:4 ). Their "defense" by the special presence of Jesus Christ is promised ( Is 4:5 , 6 ). branch-- the sprout of Jehovah. Messiah ( Jr 23:5 ; 33:15 ; Zec 3:8 ; 6:12 ; Lu 1:78 , Margin). The parallel clause does not, as Maurer objects, oppose this; for "fruit of the earth" answers to "branch"; He shall not be a dry, but a fruit-bearing branch ( Is 27:6 ; Eze 34:23-27 ). He is "of the earth" in His birth and death, while He is also "of the Lord" (Jehovah) ( Joh 12:24 ). His name, "the Branch," chiefly regards His descent from David, when the family was low and reduced ( Lu 2:4 , 7, 24); a sprout with more than David's glory, springing as from a decayed tree ( Is 11:1 ; 53:2 ; Re 22:16 ). excellent-- ( He 1:4 ; 8:6 ). comely-- ( So 5:15 , 16 ; Eze 16:14 ). escaped of Israel-- the elect remnant ( Ro 11:5 ); ( 1 ) in the return from Babylon; (2) in the escape from Jerusalem's destruction under Titus; (3) in the still future assault on Jerusalem, and deliverance of "the third part"; events mutually analogous, like concentric circles (Zec 12:2-10; 13:8, 9, &c.; 14:2; Eze 39:23-29 ; Joe 3:1-21 ).

Primarily, in the register kept of Israel's families and tribes.<div eID="gen13439" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13440" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">living--</hi>not "blotted out" from the registry, as dead; but written there as among the "escaped of Israel" (<reference osisRef="Dan.12.1">Da 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.9">Eze 13:9</reference>). When--</hi>that is, After.<div eID="gen13441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13442" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">washed--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Zech.13.1">Zec 13:1</reference>).<div eID="gen13442" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13443" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">filth--</hi>moral (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.21-Isa.1.25">Is 1:21-25</reference>).<div eID="gen13443" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13444" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">daughters of Zion--</hi>same as in <reference osisRef="Isa.3.16">Is 3:16</reference>.<div eID="gen13444" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13445" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">purged--</hi>purified by judgments; destroying the ungodly, correcting and refining the godly.<div eID="gen13445" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13446" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">blood--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.1.15">Is 1:15</reference>).<div eID="gen13446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13447" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spirit--</hi>Whatever God does in the universe, He does by His Spirit, "without the hand" of man (<reference osisRef="Job.34.20">Job 34:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.104.30">Psa 104:30</reference>). Here He is represented using His power as Judge.<div eID="gen13447" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13448" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">burning--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Matt.3.11">Mt 3:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.3.12">12</reference>). The same Holy Ghost, who sanctifies believers by the fire of affliction (Mal 3:2, 3), dooms unbelievers to the fire of perdition (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.13-1Cor.3.15">1Co 3:13-15</reference>). <div eID="gen13448" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. When-- that is, After. washed-- ( Zec 13:1 ). filth-- moral ( Is 1:21-25 ). daughters of Zion-- same as in Is 3:16 . purged-- purified by judgments; destroying the ungodly, correcting and refining the godly. blood-- ( Is 1:15 ). spirit-- Whatever God does in the universe, He does by His Spirit, "without the hand" of man ( Job 34:20 ; Psa 104:30 ). Here He is represented using His power as Judge. burning-- ( Mt 3:11 , 12 ). The same Holy Ghost, who sanctifies believers by the fire of affliction (Mal 3:2, 3), dooms unbelievers to the fire of perdition ( 1Co 3:13-15 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8388"/><div sID="gen13449" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8388"/><hi type="bold">5. create--</hi>The "new creation" needs as much God's creative omnipotence, as the material creation (<reference osisRef="2Cor.4.6">2Co 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.10">Ep 2:10</reference>). So it shall be in the case of the Holy Jerusalem to come (<reference osisRef="Isa.65.17">Is 65:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.65.18">18</reference>).<div eID="gen13449" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13450" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon--</hi>The pillar of cloud stood over the tabernacle, as symbol of God's favor and presence (<reference osisRef="Exod.13.21">Ex 13:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.13.22">22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.91.1">Psa 91:1</reference>). Both on individual families ("every dwelling") and on the general sacred "assemblies" (<reference osisRef="Lev.23.2">Le 23:2</reference>). The "cloud" became a "fire" by night in order to be seen by the Lord's people.<div eID="gen13450" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13451" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon all the glory--</hi>"upon the glorious whole"; namely, the Lord's people and sanctuary [Maurer]. May it not mean, "Upon whatever the glory (the Shekinah spoken of in the previous clause) shall rest, there shall be a defense." The symbol of His presence shall ensure also safety. So it was to Israel against the Egyptians at the Red Sea (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.19">Ex 14:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.14.20">20</reference>). So it shall be to literal Jerusalem hereafter (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.5">Zec 2:5</reference>). Also to the Church, the spiritual "Zion" (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.18">Is 32:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.33.15-Isa.33.17">33:15-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.22">He 12:22</reference>).<div eID="gen13451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13452" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tabernacle--</hi>Christ's body (<reference osisRef="John.1.14">Joh 1:14</reference>). "The word 'tabernacled' (Greek for 'dwelt') among us" (<reference osisRef="John.2.21">Joh 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.8.2">He 8:2</reference>). It is a "shadow from the heat" and "refuge from the storm" of divine wrath against man's sins (<reference osisRef="Isa.25.4">Is 25:4</reference>). Heat and storms are violent in the East; so that a portable tent is a needful part of a traveller's outfit. Such shall be God's wrath hereafter, from which the "escaped of Israel" shall be sheltered by Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.20">Is 26:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.26.21">21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.32.2">32:2</reference>).<div eID="gen13452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13453" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">covert--</hi>answering to "defense" (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.5">Is 4:5</reference>). The Hebrew for defense in <reference osisRef="Isa.4.5">Is 4:5</reference>, is "covering"; the lid of the ark or mercy seat was named from the same Hebrew word, caphar; the propitiatory; for it, being sprinkled with blood by the high priest once a year, on the day of atonement, covered the people typically from wrath. Jesus Christ is the true Mercy Seat, on whom the Shekinah rested, the propitiatory, or atonement, beneath whom the law is kept, as it was literally within the ark, and man is covered from the storm. The redeemed Israel shall also be, by union with Him, a tabernacle for God's glory, which, unlike that in the wilderness, shall not be taken down (<reference osisRef="Isa.38.20">Is 38:20</reference>). <chapter eID="Isa.4"/>
